answer: Each garden owns one rooted yarrow and one river gauge. To admit entrant n, every pair of earlier gardens jointly signs an unpredictable flood sample, and n's sensor records the corresponding plant-mass change; the sample is then consumed. One gauge and one plant can process only one pair per flood, preventing pooling or reuse. Entrant n needs C(n-1,2) plant-flood slots, so k admissions consume C(k,3)=k(k-1)(k-2)/6 dedicated slots—cubic attacker cost.
